# Architecture Decision Records

Short, immutable records of decisions that are expensive to reverse. One file per
decision, numbered `ADR-NNNN-<slug>.md`. Never edit an accepted ADR — supersede it
with a new one and mark the old `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.

## ADR number allocation

ADR numbers are drawn from **per-lane reserved ranges**; a lane never allocates
against the shared high-water mark. This removes the last-writer-wins race that
made this file a serialization point for the whole board (in one afternoon an
OP-101 card was renumbered three times and the OP-96 lane four times, each cycle
costing a rebase, a CI run and often a re-review). The rule, its rationale and
the rejected alternatives are recorded in
[ADR-0300](ADR-0300-adr-number-range-allocation-policy.md).

- The orchestrator is the **allocator**. It assigns each lane (`OP-<n>`) a
  disjoint range of numbers up front — before any of that lane's cards are
  dispatched — and writes the range into every card body of the lane.
- A lane takes its next ADR number as the **next unused number inside its own
  range** (a lane-local counter). It never consults `origin/main`'s high-water
  mark, the tail of this file, or another lane's refs.
- A new lane's block starts **above the highest in-flight range end** —
  `max(range ends in flight) + 1`, never `max(consumed number) + 1`: a lane's
  `Next free` cell is a consumed count, not its reservation bound
  ([ADR-0300 §10](ADR-0300-adr-number-range-allocation-policy.md)).
- A reserved range is **exclusive to its holder**, gaps included. A dependent
  ticket (one whose story builds on the holder's code) continues its parent
  lane's range; an independent ticket gets its own block.
- Ranges are disjoint by construction and are never re-cut, so two lanes cannot
  collide even though neither inspects the other's branches.
- Gaps inside a range (and ranges that go unused) are expected and cheap: a
  number is consumed once and is never reissued to another lane.
- Numbers allocated **before this policy** (`≤ 0145`) are frozen history and are
  never moved; a branch that already carries one keeps it.
- Board-wide / process decisions that belong to no single lane draw from the
  allocator-owned `board-wide` range.

_The **board-wide** [`0308`](ADR-0308-one-owner-per-branch-landing.md) record gained a **§Recurrence** section (card `t_1deaf426`, orchestrator; branch `OP-111-task-adr-0308-recurrence`) after the OP-111 GREEN landing (`t_71cc5e0c`, PR #352) reproduced the one-owner hazard in a new, **run-level** shape — a live implementer worker mutated the lane worktree after its handoff while the review run owned the same path. No number is consumed: the block cell stays `0311`._

_The **board-wide / process** [ADR-0312](ADR-0312-same-lane-adr-card-serialization.md) record takes `0312`, the range slot the allocator reserved at card creation (card `t_851ad543`, decided by the orchestrator card `t_78773f59`, branch `OP-112-task-same-lane-adr-serialization` off `origin/main` `a2de1a2`), and the block cell advances `0312` → `0313`. It records the rule the intra-lane number collision kept outrunning after [ADR-0300](ADR-0300-adr-number-range-allocation-policy.md) removed the cross-lane one: §7, §8 and §9 are **read-side** rules, so two cards of one lane claimed in the same dispatcher tick enumerate the same snapshot and mint the same integer — which is what happened at `0584`, where `t_48a8e8ce` (PR [#377](https://github.com/yahodu/openpic-webapp/pull/377), landed first) and `t_c469c799` (renumbered to `0585` by comment) both minted `ADR-0584` off the trunk cut `c055cac`, the fourth recurrence of a class already seen at `0147`, `0382`/`0383`+`0384` and `0482`. The decision is **rule C**: same-lane ADR-minting cards are serialized by the task graph — the successor is a `parents=[…]` child of its predecessor and reads its number off the merged trunk, so there is no concurrent sibling to enumerate — with the allocator, worker and reviewer contracts and the two rejected alternatives (a reserve-first trunk ledger edit; a `reserved:` marker in this file checked by the guard) recorded in the ADR. No number outside `0300`–`0319` is touched._

_The **board-wide / process** [ADR-0967](ADR-0967-merged-lane-local-branch-deletion.md) record takes `0967` — a **pool draw**, because the block `0300`–`0319` is exhausted (ADR-0300 §11 item 18) — and advances the `unallocated (future lanes)` cursor `0967` → `0968`. Card `t_84e8d0ed` (orchestrator; branch `OP-101-task-local-head-hygiene-rule`, worktree `.worktrees/t_84e8d0ed`) decided it after the population of unheld local-only heads regrew three times in one morning: PR [#872](https://github.com/yahodu/openpic-webapp/pull/872) (`5add954d`), PR [#873](https://github.com/yahodu/openpic-webapp/pull/873) (`867665c9`) and PR [#874](https://github.com/yahodu/openpic-webapp/pull/874) (`92701608`), each head left behind by the squash-merge that deleted its remote branch (`delete_branch_on_merge: true`). The rule is the merge step's own last act — archive the tip into `refs/prhead/<n>`, release the holding worktree, then `git update-ref -d refs/heads/<head> <sha>`, gated on the PR being `MERGED`, the tip being served verbatim by `refs/pull/<n>/head` or already an ancestor of `main`, the branch being local-only, no worktree holding it and no **other** live board row naming it — with an explicit exception for a deliberately unmerged PR (the RED-by-design pin), which keeps its branch and its worktree. Because `0967` was also the cell value of the `OP-129` and `OP-136` lanes, both cells advance to `0968` in the same edit (ADR-0300 §11 item 27's mechanism; no cell is lowered). The checklist change — `AGENTS.md` §2.3, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` §9 and the reviewer profile's own merge checklist — is routed as a follow-up card from `t_84e8d0ed`. No range is re-cut._

_The **OP-134** TEST card `t_f553e539` (Low; branch `OP-134-task-attendee-claim-i2-ttl`, worktree `.worktrees/op134-attendee-claim-i2-ttl`) is a **pool draw** — the OP-134 lane holds no reserved row, so ADR-0300 §11 item 18 sends it to the `unallocated (future lanes)` cursor, which [ADR-0967](ADR-0967-merged-lane-local-branch-deletion.md) left at `0968`, and the record takes `0968`, advancing that cursor together with the `OP-129 attendee identity lane`, the `OP-136 jobs lane` and the `board-wide / process` cells — all four read `0968` — to **`0969`**; no cell is lowered and no range is re-cut. [ADR-0968](ADR-0968-op134-attendee-claim-i2-clock.md) repairs the trunk flake that reddened the docs-only PR [#876](https://github.com/yahodu/openpic-webapp/pull/876)'s `ci` at 12:20:37Z (`AssertionError: expected 404 to be 401` in `attendee-claim.test.ts` `I2`): the case lapsed a session's `expireAt` 60 s into the **real** past, so `attendee_sessions_expire_at_ttl` (`{expireAt: 1}`, `expireAfterSeconds: 0`) could delete the row before the request, and the claim then answered `not_found` (`404`) instead of the contractual `attendee_session_expired` (`401`) — measured, the sweep landed 55.778 s after the lapse and the claim answered `{"status":404,"code":"not_found"}`. The repair keeps `expireAt` 60 s in the real **future** (no monitor pass can select it) and moves the process clock onto the instant for the request (`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["Date"] })` + `vi.setSystemTime`, the seam `attendee-sessions.test.ts` `I4` already uses), asserting the row is present at the act; the fixture helper's past-dated two-argument `lapseSession` is replaced by `lapseSession(app, token, expireAt)`. Rejected with measurements: a route-threaded injectable clock (the route passes none and the service forwards none — a `fixedClock` one minute past expiry still answered `claimed`), a bounded row-existence re-seed (the loss is a scheduled 60 s pass, so the bound only re-prices the flake), and a two-outcome discriminator (`404` is not contractual for a lapsed session; [ADR-0780](ADR-0780-op129-anonymous-attendee-sessions-red.md) requires the re-create answer). No production file, index, retention setting or other spec in the diff._

[ADR-0972](ADR-0972-op101-member-audit-log-write-green.md) is the implementation [ADR-0970](ADR-0970-op101-member-audit-logs-write.md) §Consequences routed behind its pin pack: the new module `apps/web/src/server/audit/audit-log.ts` (`auditExpireAt` — a new `Date` exactly 400 days on, `at` untouched; `requestAuditActor` — the caller id plus salted 64-hex `ipHash`/`uaHash` digests, never the raw address or agent; `writeAuditLog(session, entry)` — one `insertOne` into `COLLECTIONS.auditLogs` with the caller's session and one clock read for `at`/`expireAt`), and both handlers in `…/tenants/[tenantId]/members/[userId]/route.ts` running the membership `updateOne` and `writeAuditLog` in **one** `withTransaction` callback with `{ session }` on each operation, `PATCH` writing `member.role_changed` (`{role}` before/after) and `DELETE` writing `member.removed` (`{status}` / `{status: "removed"}`). The two log lines ([ADR-0288](ADR-0288-op101-tenant-members-residual-pins.md) R2), the `200`/`204` shapes, the gate order and the `404`/`403`/`409` arms are byte-identical; no other route, `members.ts` or schema line changed, since §20.2 already unions `member.role_changed`. A failed audit insert aborts the mutation and answers `500 internal_error` (§D3), so a `200`/`204` is evidence of both writes. Measured: focused integration `45 passed (45)`, unit `2 passed (2)`, full unit `3356 passed | 3 skipped (3359)` over 197 files, full integration `1786 passed (1786)` over 165 files, `pnpm typecheck` exit `0`, `pnpm lint` 0 errors, `prettier --check` clean, eight `adr-*` guards green. The delivered pack pins the audit-failure direction only (and `DELETE`'s transaction not at all), so the failed-*membership* arm for both verbs is routed to `t_0250ac11`, which runs on this tree. Hotspot: `docs/adr/README.md` (row `0972`; no cell edited), which the sibling ADR cards also append to — merge as a union keeping the highest value in every cell._

_The **OP-101** follow-up TEST card `t_0250ac11` (Low; branch `OP-101-task-audit-transaction-pins`, worktree `.worktrees/t_5f145f2a-audit-txn-pins`) is a **pool draw** — the OP-101 lane holds no reserved row, so ADR-0300 §11 item 18 sends it to the `unallocated (future lanes)` cursor — and it takes **`0974`**, the allocation its card body carried at creation: the sweep at this cut (`origin/main` head `1eb1ee84`) reads `0970`–`0973` on the trunk, no `ADR-097[4-9]` path in `git rev-list --objects --all -- docs/adr`, none in any `.worktrees/*/docs/adr` tree, none in the only open PR head (#895, a docs PR), and no non-`done` card holding `0974`; the four cells that a pool draw moves together (`board-wide / process`, `OP-129 attendee identity lane`, `OP-136 jobs lane`, `unallocated (future lanes)`) read `0974` and advance to **`0975`** — no cell is lowered and no range is re-cut. [ADR-0974](ADR-0974-op101-audit-txn-failed-membership-pins.md) pins the **reverse half** of [ADR-0970](ADR-0970-op101-member-audit-logs-write.md) §D3 that [ADR-0971](ADR-0971-op101-member-audit-log-write-pins.md) `T4` left open: when the **membership** write fails, no `auditLogs` row may survive, on both verbs. The measured gap was that a `PATCH` writing its audit row **outside** the transaction satisfied the whole previous pack (`45 passed (45)`) while leaving an orphan row (`{"status":500,"auditRows":1}` against the intended `0`), and `DELETE`'s transaction was not pinned at all. The repair appends `R1`/`R2` (`+182/−0`, every shipped case and helper byte-identical) with a stub on `Collection.prototype.updateOne` that rejects only `tenantMembers` with a non-transient `code: 91` driver error and forwards every other collection to the driver: `500 internal_error`, the membership `role`/`status` **and** its pre-call `updatedAt` intact, and no row for the workspace; then the stub is restored and the same call must answer `200`/`204` and write exactly one row (the anti-vacuity half). The **negative control** is measured, not asserted: moving the audit write out of the transaction reddened exactly `R1` (`AssertionError: expected [ { …(9) } ] to deeply equal []`, `Tests 1 failed | 46 passed (47)`) and the same move for `DELETE` reddened exactly `R2`, with `T1`–`T4` and every shipped case still green. No production file, no shipped assertion and no ADR-0288 R2 line is in the diff; ordering *inside* the transaction stays free. **Ledger flag, not this card's:** the round-1 reviewer recommended re-issuing `t_7aedaced` as `0974`, which this card drew, so that card must draw `0975`+ — the allocator owns the re-issue. Hotspot: `docs/adr/README.md` (row `0974`, four cells), which the sibling ADR cards also append to — merge as a union keeping the highest value in every cell._

_The **OP-101** follow-up decision card `t_7aedaced` (Low; branch `OP-101-task-billing-downgrade-audit`, worktree `.worktrees/t_7aedaced`) is a **pool draw** — the OP-101 lane holds no reserved row, so ADR-0300 §11 item 18 sends it to the `unallocated (future lanes)` cursor — and it takes **`0975`**, not the `0973` its card body carried: `0973` landed on the trunk ([ADR-0973](ADR-0973-op134-attendee-sessions-ttl-clock.md), OP-134 lane) and `0974` landed while this card waited ([ADR-0974](ADR-0974-op101-audit-txn-failed-membership-pins.md), card `t_0250ac11`, PR [#897](https://github.com/yahodu/openpic-webapp/pull/897)). The four-surface sweep at this cut (`origin/main` `d2a5467b`) finds no `ADR-0975` on the trunk, in any `.worktrees/*/docs/adr` tree, in `git rev-list --objects --all -- docs/adr`, on either open PR head (#899, #896) or in any non-`done` card's `Consumes`, so this record draws `0975` and advances the four cells that read `0975` (`board-wide / process`, `OP-129 attendee identity lane`, `OP-136 jobs lane`, `unallocated (future lanes)`) to **`0976`**; no cell is lowered and no range is re-cut. [ADR-0975](ADR-0975-op101-billing-downgrade-audit-write.md) decides the billing half [ADR-0970](ADR-0970-op101-member-audit-logs-write.md) routed on purpose: §20.2's `subscription.downgraded` is **kept** and the code is made to write it, but at the **transition** rather than the request — the two shipped paths that actually reduce `activePlanKey` (`runScheduledPlanChanges`, `runDunning`) write one row each, through the shipped seam, in the transition's own transaction, with `actor.kind: "system"` and `reason`, while `POST …/billing/downgrade` keeps its log line and writes nothing, because a schedule is intent and three shipped paths clear `scheduledChange` without ever applying it (`scheduled-change/route.ts:44`, `upgrade/route.ts:364`, `checkout/route.ts:330`). The dunning half amends `billing-crons.test.ts` `I1`'s whole-database diff deliberately (`audit_logs` joins `domain_events` and `subscriptions`; the six content collections must stay absent, so C6 is still proven structurally) and corrects `dunning.ts`'s "writes nothing else" docblock. The request-side gap the sweep found — §3.3 promises `billing.plan.downgrade_scheduled` and the route emits no domain event, so the requester is durable nowhere — is routed as its own decision card, not absorbed. Routed: RED `t_e3bb5425` (`Consumes: 0976`), its GREEN `t_6634feb1` (`Consumes: 0977`) gated on it, and the request-side decision `t_d421271e` (`Consumes: 0978`). Hotspot: `docs/adr/README.md` (row `0975`, four cells), which the sibling ADR cards also append to — merge as a union keeping the highest value in every cell._

_The **OP-101** TEST card `t_7df4b288` (Low; branch `OP-101-task-downgrade-scheduled-event`, worktree `.worktrees/op101-downgrade-scheduled-event-red`) is a **pool draw** — the OP-101 lane holds no reserved row, so ADR-0300 §11 item 18 sends it to the `unallocated (future lanes)` cursor — and it takes **`0979`**, the number its card body carried: the sweep at this cut (`origin/main` `c291cd08`, the ADR-0978 squash) finds no `ADR-0979` on the trunk (highest `0978`), in any `.worktrees/*/docs/adr` tree (highest `0978`), in `git rev-list --objects --all -- docs/adr` (`0976`–`0978`), on any open PR head (#905 `0978`, #904 `0978`, #896 `0973`) or in any non-`done` card's `Consumes` (`0977` in `t_6634feb1`, `0979` in this card, `0980` in the gated GREEN `t_ddd87497`), so this record draws `0979` and advances the four cells that read `0979` (`board-wide / process`, `OP-129 attendee identity lane`, `OP-136 jobs lane`, `unallocated (future lanes)`) to **`0980`**; no cell is lowered and no range is re-cut. _The **OP-101** review follow-up TEST card `t_dd0046f3` (Medium; branch `OP-101-task-downgrade-actor-scope-pins`, worktree `.worktrees/t_dd0046f3`) is a **pool draw** — the OP-101 lane holds no reserved row, so ADR-0300 §11 item 18 sends it to the `unallocated (future lanes)` cursor — and it takes **`0981`**: the sweep at this cut (`origin/main` `45a0d43d`) finds no `ADR-0981` on the trunk (highest `0980`), in any `.worktrees/*/docs/adr` tree (only this card's own worktree), in `git rev-list --objects --all -- docs/adr` (highest `0980`), on either open PR head (#909 `0980`, #896 none) or in any non-`done` card's `Consumes`, so this record advances the four cells that read `0981` (`board-wide / process`, `OP-129 attendee identity lane`, `OP-136 jobs lane`, `unallocated (future lanes)`) to **`0982`**; no cell is lowered and no range is re-cut. [ADR-0981](ADR-0981-op101-actor-exemption-audience-scope-pins.md) closes finding **F1** of the post-merge review of [ADR-0980](ADR-0980-op101-downgrade-scheduled-event-green.md): [ADR-0979](ADR-0979-op101-downgrade-scheduled-event-pins.md) `D1`–`D3` pinned the payer's own delivery only on the type that motivated the exemption, so a `typeKey`-scoped variant of the spare still read `15 passed (15)` — measured. The repair adds one integration spec, `billing-plan-upgraded-delivery.test.ts` (2 cases, no production file), and pins the discriminator on `billing.plan.upgraded`, the only other `BILLING`-audience type emitted with a user actor: the owner who **is** the billing contact receives exactly one in-app row and one rendered, `sent` email (`F1D`, guarded by the outbox row reading `pending` before the drain and `done` afterwards), while a **different** billing contact receives it and the owner-actor does not (`F1E`, the sibling of the downgrade spec's `D2` one type over). Measured: `2 passed (2)` on the shipped tree, and `1 failed | 16 passed (17)` against the `typeKey`-scoped variant — `F1D` alone, `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`, with the downgrade spec's fifteen still green. Two items were **measured and routed, not pinned**: an **absent** `currentPeriodEnd` (not `null`, which the route's stored schema rejects with a `500`, `expected date, received null`) makes each identical downgrade request mint a fresh `now`, so two requests deliver `2` events, `2` feed rows and `2` emails; and eight concurrent double-submit rounds each answered `[200, 200]` with one event, which is **not** the `500` ADR-0980 §Consequences records as settled — a decision-level contradiction, and a timing-dependent outcome either way._

| [0669](ADR-0669-op121-bounded-wait-extracted.md)                                   | OP-121 refactor (F2/F3/F4 of the review of `t_ed6d5933`, behaviour-preserving): the bounded wait becomes **one** module, `@/server/db/retry-wait` (`RIVAL_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 1_000`, `RIVAL_COMMIT_POLL_MS = 25`, `sleep`, `waitForCommitted(read, isSettled)`), with both call sites — `rivalDecisionCommitted` and `rivalRemovalCommitted` — delegating and keeping their predicates byte-for-byte, so the pair cannot drift. The ceiling now bounds the **wait**, not the poll count: the loop sleeps only when another poll follows, so the last check lands at `1 000 ms` (41 reads) instead of the `1 025 ms` the trailing sleep cost, and the documented ceiling equals the measured one. The poll stays linear — a backoff would answer a late-committing winner later, and the pinned pair's hold is 100 ms — and the failure path's **41 sequential reads** are recorded in §Consequences rather than engineered away. The pin spec is not edited; `E1`, `I5` and `R2` reach every arm of the helper. | [0806](ADR-0806-op132-confirm-publication-green.md)                                | OP-132 GREEN (F3, Medium): the three ADR-0805 pins made true with **no test, fixture or mock edited** — the diff is the confirm route, the record and this ledger. The confirmation is the only emitter of `attendee.matches.new` that **ships at this head** — a grep over `apps/` and `packages/` finds the catalogue entry and the confirm route and nothing else — and the ADR-0805 pin constrains **how many** deliveries one activation result yields, never **who** publishes: its emptiness assertion reads after `runWorker` → `finishSelfieWorker` writes the already-active row's embedding and matches with raw driver calls, so it observed an absence and forbade no publisher (ADR-0808 §2). A late worker result is therefore announced only by a second, **client-initiated** confirm that no shipped client-facing text asks for — the `200` body's `pollUrl` is the read-only `GET …/me` of §6.4, which emits no domain event — and ADR-0808 §1 assigns that publication to the **pipeline**: `POST /api/v1/internal/domain-events` (OP-135 §1, `dedupeKey` honoured) for the event, `POST /api/v1/internal/worker/report` (OP-135 §3) for `status`/`matchCount`/`lastMatchRunAt`, and `pipeline-sweep` step 4 (OP-136 §2) for the run, with **neither endpoint shipping at this head**. The delivery's `count` becomes the rows **this selfie** produced (`countDocuments({ profileId, selfieId })`, §17.5's `selfieId`) rather than the profile total, while `matchCount` keeps the §6.4 total, so A's 3 and B's 2 add up to 5; the anchor cannot tie on a timestamp, which the parent record's watermark near-fix can. Idempotency comes from a deterministic `dedupeKey` — `attendee.matches.new:<eventId>:<profileId>:<selfieId>`, the §10.3.2 shape the codebase already mints — **read before the insert**, because a colliding insert inside a transaction aborts it (measured: `withTransaction` exhausted three retries and the repeat answered `500 internal_error`/`TransactionRetryLimitError`), and the unique partial index stays the concurrency backstop; §15.3's `firstMatchNotifiedAt` is stamped by the first delivery inside the same transaction. The seven-key `200` envelope, the five existing status codes and the single-event behaviour for a single confirm are unchanged. Recorded known limit: one delivery per activation result, so a worker **re-run** for an already-announced selfie cannot re-announce through the confirmation (those arrivals belong to the pipeline's own `attendee.matches.new`/`matches.ready` path). Draws `0806` — the sweep was empty (no worktree, local branch or open PR carries `0806`; the trunk's newest is `0804`); both cells advance to `0807`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Accepted                                                                                                                     |

| [0808](ADR-0808-op132-late-match-publication-ownership.md)                         | OP-132 decision (test-only, `t_b0bf2ff2` decision **(a)**): the **pipeline** publishes a match result that lands **after** the confirmation, and one activation result has exactly **one** delivery identity — `attendee.matches.new:<eventId>:<profileId>:<selfieId>` — so whichever publisher writes first the other is a no-op. Ownership is the worker's `POST /api/v1/internal/domain-events` (OP-135 §1, `dedupeKey` honoured) for the event and `POST /api/v1/internal/worker/report` (OP-135 §3) for `status`/`matchCount`/`lastMatchRunAt`, with the incremental run produced by `pipeline-sweep` step 4 (OP-136 §2, `match_incremental`); **neither endpoint ships at this head** (`apps/web/src/app/api/v1/internal/` holds only `cron/`; OP-135/OP-136 are `todo`), so a late result is announced only by a second, client-initiated confirm that no client-facing text asks for — which is the one fact ADR-0806 §1 got right, and the record is corrected here for the two it did not. ADR-0805 §3's "the pins would not forbid it" was self-contradictory only because case 3's emptiness assertion looked like a prohibition: `runWorker` → `finishSelfieWorker` (`apps/web/src/test/helpers/selfie-flow.ts:638`) writes the embedding and the matches with **raw driver calls**, so nothing production ran and the assertion could not fail — the pins constrain **how many** deliveries one activation result yields, never **who** writes them. Case 3 therefore becomes two cases: the load-bearing one publishes the pipeline's row first through `emitDomainEvent` with the shared identity, then confirms and asserts the surviving row is the pipeline's own (`emitted.id`) with `status: "ready"`, `matchCount: 3`, one row and no second emit on a further confirm; a throwaway `dedupeKey` shape change in the confirm reddens exactly that case (`expected [ { …(10) }, { …(10) } ] to have a length of 1 but got 2`, restored byte-identically), so the pin discriminates the key shape and nothing else; the second case keeps ADR-0805 §3's recovery content as the confirmation's **own** contract, not the designed recovery and not a client instruction. A later **arrival** for an already-announced selfie is a different delivery whose key must carry the run (the incremental run id or its `createdAt`), never `selfieId` alone, or the unique partial index swallows it — that key belongs to OP-136. Rejected: (b) the client re-confirms (the poll is a read-only `GET …/me`, §6.4 projects no unannounced-matches field, and it leaves the anonymous attendee uncovered by design) and (c) the confirmation as the only publisher (leaves §7.6's "additional matches later" with no producer and `firstMatchNotifiedAt` owned by nobody) — although (c) is the accurate description of this head, which §1 records explicitly. No production change in this repo: the confirm's pre-read already makes the two publishers mutually exclusive; the one in-repo touch is the route docblock (GREEN sibling `t_29382bcc`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Accepted                                                                                                                     |

Measured on `origin/main` `2c278191`: `GET /me/data-requests/{id}` admits the session that filed the row, but that session is a **30-day** credential — `retention.attendeeSessionDays` (`platform-settings.ts:387`) equals `compliance.slaDays` — so after `expireAt` the resolver throws `attendee_session_expired`, after the TTL monitor deletes the row the route answers `401 unauthenticated`, and a re-created session is a new `_id` and therefore `404`; `dataSubjectRequests` has **no TTL** (`indexes.ts:604`–`636`), so the record outlives every credential that could read it, the attendee has no email or phone on file (§1.5 makes them "deliberately unreachable by notifications"), and `GET /me/data-requests` was `requireAuth("user")` (ADR-0902 §9 residual). The decision: an attendee filing answers `pollUrl: "/api/v1/me/data-requests/<id>?receipt=<token>"` and a user filing keeps the bare path, the receipt keeping its **six keys** with the token inside `pollUrl`; format `base64url(payload) + "." + lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256(base64url(payload))` over `{"v":1,"kind":"dsr_receipt","requestId":"<24-hex>"}`, keyed with a domain-separated subkey (`"dsr-receipt:v1"`) of `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` — no new env var, no new setting, no column, no collection, no TTL change; **no `exp`**, because the token's lifetime is the row's; a valid token for another id is `404 not_found`, a bad signature or malformed payload is `401 unauthenticated`, never `403`; the receipt is resolved **before** the attendee session so a stale `op_att` cookie cannot shadow it; and it reads one request, lists nothing and files nothing. §8.1 gains the auth line and the six receipt rules, §1.5 one cross-reference bullet, and the re-issue path is stated to be absent. Four appended integration cases in `data-subject-requests.test.ts` (`+297/−0`; the shipped 39, every helper and the harness byte-identical): **I28** the six keys plus `?receipt=` with the decoded-then-re-encoded payload and the bare-path user arm; **I29** the receipt alone reading a row whose `attendeeSessions` row is deleted, the dangling cookie refused `unauthenticated`, and the lapsed cookie losing to the receipt while its own read stays `attendee_session_expired`; **I30** another id `404`, a flipped signature character and `?receipt=garbage` `401`, no credential `401`, never `403`; **I31** both sessions' lists scoped to their own rows with the exact six-key row, no credential `401 unauthenticated`, and a receipt on the list `401`. **RED by design** and the PR stays a **draft**: `Tests 4 failed \| 39 passed (43)`, the four reds exactly `I28`–`I31` (`expected '' to match /^\?receipt=…/` twice, `expected 401 to be 200` twice), every shipped case green as the control; `tsc` 0, `eslint` 0 errors **and** 0 warnings on the spec, `prettier --check` clean, the seven `adr-*` guards green. | [0991](ADR-0991-proprietary-license.md)                                            | Board-wide (card `t_a3351538`; **pool draw** `Consumes: 0991`, the board-wide cell; branch `OP-101-task-readme-contributing-and-license`): the repository gains a **proprietary** license, a contribution grant that keeps a future relicensing possible, and the dependency-license audit that clears it. `LICENSE` (OpenPic Proprietary License 1.0) permits viewing, local evaluation and short quotation, and forbids — by name — hosting or running the app as a service whether paid or free, distribution whether paid or free, modification, sublicensing, trademark use and notice removal; §11 states the license may be replaced for future releases, and §6 takes a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable and sublicensable grant from every contributor, expressly including the right to relicense, plus a patent grant — without it a contributor's copyright would veto the change the owner requires. `CONTRIBUTING.md` carries the workflow for humans and agents (branch and commit format, the TDD iron law, the conventions table, ADR numbering, review and merge gates, contribution terms, the security route); `README.md` carries the front door (three planes, features, stack, layout, getting started, scripts, testing, API at a glance, documentation index); `package.json` gains `license: UNLICENSED`. Audit at this cut, `pnpm licenses list --json`: 542 packages, 210 of them production, **zero** GPL/AGPL/SSPL/BUSL/EUPL/OSL/CC-BY-NC, and exactly three with conditions — `MPL-2.0` `lightningcss` and its `linux-x64-gnu` binary (Next's CSS compiler, unmodified), `CC-BY-4.0` `caniuse-lite` (build-time data, attribution only) and `LGPL-3.0-or-later` `@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64` (transitive `next` → `sharp`, an unmodified native binary loaded at runtime in a service deployment, so the relink obligation is not triggered) — so no dependency forbids a proprietary license. Rejected: MIT/Apache-2.0 (grants what the owner forbids), BUSL (converts to open source on a date nobody chose), CC-BY-NC (not a software license, no patent grant), no `LICENSE` file (the same position, undocumented and unable to carry a grant). Recorded platform limit: GitHub's terms let any user fork a public repository; the license makes that use a breach, it does not prevent the fork. Only a `Date`, a string or a number may name an instant — a `joinedAt: true` row silently served `1970-01-01T00:00:00.001Z` at the base tree, which is why the pins constrain the accepted kinds and not merely the absence of a throw. The decision is unchanged (the offset-bearing form is still neither UTC nor ms precision); the pin drives that shape. New spec `apps/web/src/test/integration/payments-cashfree-expiresat.test.ts` (MSW): I1 asserts, per row and **on the input itself**, that the vendor string is offset-bearing with neither ms nor `Z` (so the pin cannot be weakened to an ISO-ms fixture) and that `expiresAt` comes back as the RFC 3339 UTC ms `Z` value (`2025-06-01T10:20:12+05:30` → `2025-06-01T04:50:12.000Z`, the vendor docs' own example; `2100-01-01T23:00:08+05:30` → `2100-01-01T17:30:08.000Z`; the factory default `2026-11-01T10:30:46+05:30` → `2026-11-01T05:00:46.000Z`) plus the canonical regex; I2 pins that an unparseable vendor expiry rejects with `UpstreamContractError` rather than returning raw garbage (mirroring `parseWebhook`'s unparseable-`event_time` guard). The pre-existing verbatim-passthrough assertion in `payments-cashfree-adapter.test.ts` (`toBe(response.subscription_expiry_time)`) contradicted the decision and would have blocked the GREEN, so its expectation is repinned to `2026-11-01T05:00:46.000Z`; the factory fixture stays vendor-shaped, untouched. Evidence at the RED head: integration **5 failed | 5 passed (10)** — all five at assertion level against today's passthrough (`expected '2025-06-01T10:20:12+05:30' to be '2025-06-01T04:50:12.000Z'`; `expected '2026-11-01T10:30:46+05:30' to be '2026-11-01T05:00:46.000Z'`; `promise resolved "{ … }" instead of rejecting`) — `npx tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit `0`, ESLint 0 problems and `prettier --check` clean on both touched specs. **Test files only** — no production file touched, no test-mode conditional. The gated GREEN sibling `t_e2747a56` reuses this worktree and must base its branch on this pins branch. No number outside the lane range `0380`–`0399` is touched._

ADR-0320's add-on schema of record gains one field, `grantDelta` (the entitlement delta one ordered `quantity` unit grants), because it named no amount and the contract's own `storage-50gb` example (a `53687091200`-byte grant) was not otherwise expressible. [ADR-0680](ADR-0680-op122-queue-port-red.md) fixes the executable contract the card left open: `@/server/queue/envelope` (`queueEnvelopeSchema` as a **strict** `z.strictObject` over the ten §10.4 pointer fields — `v: 1`, the three work kinds, 24-hex `id`/`tenantId`/`eventId`, `high|normal`, non-empty `spaceKey`, ISO `enqueuedAt`, non-negative integer `attempt`, non-empty `traceId` — plus the two total mappings `queueKeyFor(priority)` `high = q:selfie` / `normal = q:image` and `defaultPriorityFor(kind)` `selfie|match_incremental = high` / `event_image = normal`), `@/server/queue/work-queue` (the `enqueue`/`claim`/`ack`/`nack` port with `provider` on the port, so `queueRef.provider` is taken from the selected adapter), `@/server/adapters/upstash-queue` (`createUpstashQueue({url, token, logger?, fetch?})` — one `POST` of `["LPUSH", queueKey, JSON.stringify(envelope)]` with the bearer token, the answer Zod-parsed to `{result: number}`, a changed shape or a non-JSON body = non-retryable `UpstreamContractError` **plus** an `error` record `queue.upstream_contract_violation` carrying `provider: "upstash"`, `operation: "enqueue"` and the `queueKey`, and a 5xx classified through the shared `classifyTransportFailure` as a **retryable** `TransportError` with no drift record), `@/server/adapters/memory-queue` (`memoryWorkQueue({clock?})` — FIFO claim per key, an in-flight message never redelivered, `ack` permanent, `nack(msg, delaySeconds)` claimable again only after the injected clock's delay, and an inspectable `outbox`), and `@/server/queue/enqueue-work` (`enqueueWork({db, queue, collection, work, logger?, clock?})` builds the envelope itself, writes **only** `processing.queueRef = {queueKey, provider, messageId}` on success, and on an enqueue failure logs `warn` `queue.enqueue_failed` with the `queueKey` and the `kind`, never throws, and returns `{enqueued: false}` so the item stays `queued` for the sweep). This RED delivers **test files only** — two unit specs (`queue-envelope.test.ts` 20 cases, `queue-memory-adapter.test.ts` 8 cases), one integration spec (`queue-upstash.test.ts` 8 cases) and the fixture `src/test/factories/queue.ts` — plus this ADR and the README ledger rows; the five throwaway stubs used to prove type-correctness were deleted and `git status` shows the four test files only. Evidence: with wrong-semantics stubs `tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exited `0` and the unit probe ran **26 failed | 15 passed (41)**, every failure assertion-level (`expected the schema to reject an extra "payload" field: expected true to be false`, `expected 'q:image' to be 'q:selfie'`, `expected 'normal' to be 'high'`); a faithful throwaway implementation then made the unit specs **41 passed (41)** and the integration spec **8 passed (8)**, so the contract is satisfiable as written. Mutation probes on that implementation proved the integration pins load-bearing: dropping the Zod validation reddens the drift case (`expected ZodError: […] to be an instance of UpstreamContractError`), hard-coding `provider` and advancing `processing.status` reddens both happy paths (`expected 'processing' to be 'queued'`), and rethrowing the enqueue failure reddens the non-fatal case (`TransportError: Transport request failed with status 500`) — **4 failed | 4 passed (8)** in total, every file restored by deletion. At handoff both projects are red as the honest missing modules (`@/server/queue/envelope`, `@/server/adapters/memory-queue`, `@/server/adapters/upstash-queue`, `@/server/queue/enqueue-work`); `prettier --check` clean and ESLint 0 errors on every touched file. The GREEN owes the `@/server/queue/work-queue` port module, a `claim`/`ack`/`nack` wire choice of its own (list vs sorted set, and how a claim returns a message id) recorded in its own ADR, and it must base its branch on this pins branch, not bare `origin/main`. `docs/adr/README.md` is the known shared-ledger hotspot: the `0680`/`0681` cells and the pool's `0700`+ merge as a union keeping the highest values. No number outside the lane range `0680`–`0699` is touched._

_The **OP-122** lane's `Next free` cell advanced from `0681` to `0682` (card `t_153091a3`, OP-122 GREEN on branch `OP-122-task-queue-port-green`). [ADR-0681](ADR-0681-op122-queue-green.md) records the implementation choices the RED left open: the Upstash wire is a **list** (`LPUSH` onto the head, `RPOP` with a typed count from the tail), message ids are adapter-minted `randomUUID`s because a list has no server-assigned id, `claim` keeps a process-local `messageId → {queueKey, payload}` ledger so `ack` retires a popped message and `nack` re-`LPUSH`es it, `nack`'s `delaySeconds` is not honoured by the list transport (marked `shortcut:` in the adapter; the port's delay semantics stay pinned on the memory adapter), and `enqueueWork` wraps the enqueue and its `processing.queueRef` write in one `try` so a broker or write failure is a `warn queue.enqueue_failed` returning `{enqueued: false}` rather than a failed user request. The `0680`/`0681` cells and the pool's `0700`+ merge as a union keeping the highest values._

[ADR-0766](ADR-0766-op128-batch-signed-media-url-refresh-red.md) fixes the batch refresh contract the card left open: `@/server/media/signed-urls` (`authorizeSignedUrlItem` — the whole per-item policy with the fixed precedence `not_found` → `authentication_required` → `feature_not_available` → `forbidden`, and `signedUrlBatchStatus` — `403` only when every item is denied **and** none is `authentication_required`) plus `POST /api/v1/media/signed-urls`. Three decisions are worth naming. **First**, the endpoint is `public`-labelled even though §5.6 says "auth `user` or `attendee`": I6 pins an anonymous request answering `200` with `denied[] {code: "authentication_required"}`, which an `attendee`/`user` label makes impossible (`requireAuth` would `401` before the handler), so per-item authorization wins and the `authentication_required` denial is exempt from the `403` escalation — otherwise a one-item anonymous `original` request would be an all-denied batch and a `403`, contradicting I6 directly. **Second**, the `413` is the handler's own check, not the schema's: zod's `.max(200)` fails through the pipeline as `422 validation_failed` (§0.6), which I4 does not accept — the probe showed `expected 413, received 422` and moving the check into the handler fixed it — and I4 also pins the inclusive boundary (exactly 200 items → `200`) so the cap cannot drift. **Third**, the §5.6 gate applies ADR-0762's `{ visibility: "visible", deletedAt: null }` on the **attendee** branch, which is the bypass that lane's F1 handed over: a hidden image that still carries a `face_matches` row for the caller is denied for both kinds while the visible matched image in the same request is signed, pinned at both levels (two `U1` rows + one integration case). `feature_not_available` reuses the entitlement service's own denial reason (§0.14, §6.6) and `payload_too_large` reuses the catalogue's `413`, so no new media code is owed. The query budget is pinned by `Collection.prototype` spies rather than vendor-shaped numbers: `reads(200) === reads(2)` and `reads(200) < 200`, after a warm-up and with both answers asserted full. Two RED spec files are the whole deliverable (`media-signed-urls-authorization.test.ts` 24 cases, `media-signed-urls.test.ts` 15 cases) plus this ADR and the ledger. Evidence: no implementation `→` exactly two `TS2307`s naming `@/server/media/signed-urls` and `@/app/api/v1/media/signed-urls/route`, both suites dying on `Cannot find package`; a naive pure stub + `500` route `→ tsc` exit 0, `unit 9 failed | 15 passed` (exactly the feature-gate, unmatched-attendee, hidden and `authentication_required`-aggregate rows) and `integration 15 failed (15)` at `expected 200, received 500`; a faithful near-fix `→ unit 24/24 and integration 15/15 green`; three mutation probes then proved the pins bite (drop the hidden predicate → `3 failed | 21 passed` and `expected [ …(3) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]`; one `findOne` per item → I5 `expected 414 to be 18`; `signedUrlBatchStatus` always `200` → `2 failed | 22 passed` and `expected 200 to be 403`), each restored byte-identically and both probe files deleted (`git status --short` shows the two specs only). Out of scope and recorded as open items: whether a **member** may refresh a hidden image (O1 — §4.4's grid signs hidden thumbnails, so either answer is defensible and the card does not name it), the `op_att` anonymous-session variant of I6 (O2 — OP-129 owns the resolver and is still `todo`, so attendee cases drive a signed-in user with `face_matches` rows, which §0.3 says satisfies the `attendee` label), the `media.sign` rate class (O3, declared but unpinned — the suite fires four requests per identity) and the `expiresAt` string form (O5). No number outside `0760`–`0779` is touched._

The card `t_8f0c9915` (Low, raised by the OP-135 DEPS verification `t_f4a45d1c`) had been told that re-running a PR's check is a refresh "because GitHub re-evaluates the merge commit against current main"; measured on this repo that is false, and it is a **red-maker**: for a `pull_request` event the job checks out the merge commit GitHub built for that event and the run keeps it, so a rerun replays the same tree. `#272` proves it — `refs/pull/272/merge` = `300fcf35` (`Merge d5be9af4… into 67feedeb…`, 2026-10-24T20:56:12Z), run `40132002880`'s `audit` job log reads `HEAD is now at 300fcf3 Merge … into 67feedeb…`, `300fcf35:pnpm-workspace.yaml` carries **no** `GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf` entry, and `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=moderate` on exactly that tree exits `1` with `1 high` and 9 paths — while the PR's `audit` check today is `SUCCESS` (2026-10-24T20:56:38Z). The record states four operative rules: stale evidence is refreshed by a **synchronize** event (push or "Update branch"), never by `gh run rerun` / `--failed`; a refresh verifies the gate and never justifies a rebase (a branch carrying a real advisory stays red); a `CONFLICTING` PR builds no merge ref on its next push, so a missing `CI`/`audit` check is **no evidence**, never green (extending [ADR-0305](ADR-0305-ci-evidence-conflicting-pr-suppression.md) §1); and whether `audit` becomes a **required** check is the sibling ruleset/backlog card `t_72d33d02`, referenced rather than decided here. It also sharpens one premise of the raising card: a merge ref left from an earlier mergeable moment survives a conflict (`#272` has one, `#545`/`#668` never did), so the ref's *existence* is not freshness — the run's own merge base is. `docs/adr/README.md` is the shared-ledger hotspot: this row, this cell and this note merge as a union keeping the higher cell (`0317`). The card `t_559f577f` (Medium, board process; evidence measured by the orchestrator card `t_f4a1695b`) records an incident the board could not prevent: on 2026-11-18 between 10:25Z and 10:46Z about 26 registered git worktrees under `.worktrees/` were removed, directory and registration together, while cards naming those paths were `todo`, `ready` or `running`, and the OP-136 shared path `.worktrees/t_16239628` — named by 8 non-terminal cards — was one of them. Every candidate reaper was measured and ruled out (completion cleanup, whose shared-use guard demonstrably fired, `kanban gc`, the worktree pruner whose dry run prints `skip-kanban` for every `t_<hex>` tree, the scratch pruner, hermes cron, host cron/systemd, the never-installed disk-cleanup plugin, gateway housekeeping, and every agent session's tool calls in the window), so the removal was an **out-of-band attended reclaim** and no board-side hook can see that surface. The record states three rules: a lane path is not durable board state, so a worker whose path is missing, empty or not a checkout of its lane rebuilds it first (attach the lane branch if one exists, else `wt/<card>` from `origin/main`, else `--detach` for a `dir`-only lane), installs its own `node_modules` and comments what it rebuilt — empty-tree execution is the failure class this closes, and it fails ambiguously rather than loudly (measured in an empty directory: a vitest startup error about the project filter, and `ERR_PNPM_NO_LOCKFILE` from the install), so the rebuild must come before any command; reclaim happens only through `hermes worktree prune` or `git worktree remove` on one named path, never a bulk `rm -rf .worktrees/*` or a `git worktree list`-driven loop, and a hand reclaim first reads `SELECT workspace_path FROM tasks WHERE status NOT IN ('done','archived','failed','cancelled')`; and whoever mints a `dir` follow-up pointing at an existing lane path verifies `test -d "$workspace_path"` at creation. The rejected alternative is **exempt kanban trees from all pruners** — rejected because the loss was out-of-band, so no pruner can be exempted; the durable fix is dispatch-time verification plus an operator rule. The cell skips two numbers because this record takes `0403` and the GREEN takes `0404` without writing a ledger row. [ADR-0403](ADR-0403-op140-upgrade-checkout-persistence.md) narrows ADR-0942 §2's billing row (`subscription` × `complete_mandate`): `POST …/billing/checkout` already persists `subscriptions.checkout = { url, expiresAt }` (`billing/checkout/route.ts:416-422`) and the `reuse` arm reads it (`server/services/subscriptions/checkout.ts:163`), but `POST …/billing/upgrade` mints its row without the field (`billing/upgrade/route.ts:336-377`, the URL returned inline at `:412-416`/`:420`) and nothing can read it back. The record fixes the contract the GREEN implements: the upgrade's `subscriptions.insertOne` stores `checkout: { url: mandate.checkoutUrl, expiresAt: new Date(mandate.expiresAt) }` — the same two fields and the same derivation the checkout path uses, no invented TTL — and `@/server/services/subscriptions` exports `readStoredCheckout({ db, subscriptionId: ObjectId }): Promise<{ url: string; expiresAt: Date } | null>`, an **id-keyed** read that answers the named row's own block and `null` for a link-less row or an unknown id. The spec `apps/web/src/test/integration/billing-stored-checkout.test.ts` (5 cases, `I1`–`I5`) drives the real route modules with the Cashfree adapter over MSW and reads back **through the barrel seam**, so no assertion inspects the stored document's shape. Evidence: at the branch point all five redden on the absent export (`@/server/services/subscriptions must export readStoredCheckout({ db, subscriptionId }) …`); with a throwaway **seam-only** near-fix `I1`/`I2` redden for the named reason (`AssertionError: expected null to deeply equal { …(2) }`) while `I3`–`I5` are green, proving the checkout arm already satisfies its side and the upgrade write is the only missing half; with the near-fix plus the two-line upgrade write the file is `5 passed (5)`; a stored `now + 86_400_000` expiry reddens `I1` alone and a `findOne({}, { sort: { updatedAt: -1 } })` seam reddens `I1`/`I2`/`I4`/`I5`. The near-fix was deleted (`git checkout --` on the two touched production files, `rm -f` on the new module) and `git status --short` shows only the spec, this record and the ledger. `pnpm typecheck` exit `0`, ESLint 0 problems, `prettier --check` clean on the spec. The reversal condition is stated in the record: when every mint path persists `checkout` and this lane's seam reads it back, the OP-140 `subscription` × `complete_mandate` arm and its pin can be written (owner: OP-140 notifications lane) — the four walled-off OP-140 files are untouched here. The `unallocated (future lanes)` pool cell stays `0420`+. No number outside the lane range `0400`–`0419` is touched._
